name: GestureRotate
summary: Like GestureScale, but the hands move the viewpoint instead of the object before a face is touched directly.
howItWorks: An eyeball-in-hand view change brings the face close for a fingertip touch. Tested with 16 participants selecting single faces on regular polyhedra (4, 6 or 12 faces, two sizes) with tracked hands.
limitations: Viewpoint motion lowered usability and caused dizziness.

relationships.note: Introduced with seven other face-selection techniques in the same study.
The study's baseline (DragRotate) rotates the object with one hand and selects with a hand ray.
